title: Entering open source projects - urlcat
summary: Most people have a dream to participate in open source projects, but they don’t know how to start the project? Today I was lucky enough to meet a library that I can start with.
markdown:
Most people have a dream to participate in open source projects, but they don’t know how to start the project? Today I was lucky enough to come across a library that I can start with — urlcat
![image]()
Untitled.png
urlcat is an open source project with only 267 lines of code, but it has gained 1.4k stars and more than 1w weekly downloads. This is the open source project with the smallest source code that I have encountered so far. Let’s take a closer look and see the role of each file in the project.
![image]()
Untitled 1.png
## .github
![image]()
image.png
Judging from the naming, they are issue and pr templates. These three templates can effectively reduce the communication cost between authors and users and solve problems efficiently. Among them:
bug_report.md description:
1. what problem
1. How to reproduce the problem
1. What is the expected behavioral effect?
1. screenshot
1. Desktop environment: what system, what browser, what version
1. Mobile phone environment: what device, what system, what browser, what version
1. Problem context: The purpose is to indicate whether the problem is related to other problems
destiny_request.md Description:
1. Is the feature you need related to a problem?
1. Describe the solution you want
1. Describe alternatives you might have considered
1. Describe prefab-related functional issues
pull_request_template.md Description:
1. Summary of PR functions
1. Detailed description of PR
## docs
![image]()
image.png
Use What, Why, and How to accurately explain the meaning of the project's existence.
- What: What is it?
- Why: Why do it?
- How: How to use
In addition, it also provides detailed API descriptions and tells everyone how to participate in the project and contribute your own code.
## src
The folder where the source code is stored. I will write a separate article about the source code later.
## test
Everyone says that unit testing is very important, but they all think that writing unit tests is time-consuming and laborious. Even if it is only a few hundred lines of code, the author still wrote such detailed unit tests. This is an attitude.
![image]()
Untitled 4.png
## .all-contributorsrc
For a project to maintain vitality and continue to develop, it requires the strength of everyone.
## .editorconfig
Helps maintain consistent coding style across different editors and IDEs.
```plain text
# 是否是顶级配置文件，设置为 true 的时候才会停止搜索.editorconfig 文件
root = true

[*]
# 换行符类型
end_of_line = lf
# 是否让文件以空行结束
insert_final_newline = true
# 缩进方式
indent_style = space
# 缩进大小
indent_size = 2
# 编码格式
charset = utf-8
```
## .eslintignore
Tell eslint to ignore specific files and directories and not instrument them.
```plain text
node_modules
dist
coverage
```
## .eslintrc.js
eslint configuration file
```javascript
module.exports = {
  env: {
    node: true,
  },
  root: true,
  parser: '@typescript-eslint/parser',
  plugins: ['@typescript-eslint'],
  extends: ['eslint:recommended', 'plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended'],
  rules: {
    'object-curly-spacing': ['error', 'always'],
    'array-bracket-spacing': ['error', 'never'],
    quotes: ['error', 'single'],
    'no-console': ['error'],
  },
};
```
There are many good articles about the configuration of eslint. If you are interested, you can read this article.
Related articles:
- ESLint configuration file.eslintrc parameter description
## .gitignore
This configuration is useful when you need to ignore some files when submitting code.
```plain text
/node_modules
/dist
/dist-test
/.nyc_output
/coverage
.vscode
```
## .npmignore
When you need to publish an npm package, you can ignore some files that do not need to be published to npm.
```plain text
/node_modules
/dist-test
/src
/docs
/test
/.travis.yml
/tsconfig.json
/tsconfig-test.json
/.nyc_output
/coverage
```
## .travis.yml
A configuration file for a continuous integration service
```yaml
language: node_jsnode_js:  - lts/*  - 14  - 13  - 12  - 11  - 10script:  - npm run lint  - npm test  - npm run coverage
```
Regarding continuous integration services, just read this article by teacher Ruan Yifeng.

## package-lock.json
To simply understand, in order to lock the version number of a third-party package, since the project will rely on a large number of third-party packages, and the third-party package will also depend on other third-party packages, when the package updates an incompatible API, after executing npm install, unexpected situations may occur when the project is running.
Related articles:
- npm semantic versioning
- The difference between package dependencies between package-lock.json and yarn.lock
## package.json
As a front-end person, I am very familiar with it. Let me share a few uncommon but critical configurations:
Specify node version number:
```json
{  "engines": {    "node": ">=8 <14"  }}
```
Specify npm version:
```json
{  "engines": {    "npm": "~1.0.20"  }}
```
If you plan to publish an npm package, the files field may be useful to specify the files to publish to npm
Hooks, npm scripts have pre and post hooks. Its role is to execute certain special commands to trigger automated scripts, such as:
- Remove dist before build
- Run unit tests and package the project before publishing
```json
"scripts": {    "clean": "shx rm -rf dist",    "prebuild": "npm run clean",    "build": "tsc -p .",    "test": "jest",    "lint": "eslint . --ext .js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx",    "coverage": "cat ./coverage/lcov.info | coveralls",    "prepublish": "npm test && npm run build",    "docs": "docsify serve docs --open"  },
```
